This empire ruled over 30 million people for a century, and not one ethnic group was ever the majority. Not Germans, not Hungarians — nobody. Here's what that patchwork actually looked like.

a thread 🧵🗺️

1/ By an 1842 count, Slavs were the largest bloc at roughly 45% — but 'Slavs' wasn't one people. It meant Czechs, Poles, Slovaks, Ukrainians, Slovenes, Croats and Serbs, none of whom individually came close to a plurality.
2/ Germans followed at around 18%, clustered in Austria proper and Bohemia's cities. Hungarians were next at roughly 15%, Italians about 13%, and Romanians around 4% in the empire's eastern corner.

3/ The map shows why Vienna never got a break: Czechs and Slovaks packed the north, Poles and Ukrainians (Rusyns) the northeast, Hungarians the broad center, Romanians the east, Italians and South Slavs the south.

4/ In 1867 Vienna stopped trying to rule it as one bloc. The Ausgleich split the empire into an Austrian half and a Hungarian half as equal partners — even though Hungarians made up only about 42% of their own half.

5/ It unraveled fast at the end. Hungary's parliament voted to end the union on 17 October 1918; within a month both Austria and Hungary had declared themselves republics, and the empire broke into the nation-states that still roughly outline Central Europe.
6/ One crown, a dozen nations who never agreed on much — the tension outlived the empire by a century. Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
